name: Seep
description: Seep is a four-player partnership fishing game played in the Punjab and other parts of India and Pakistan. Players capture cards from a layout; building piles called houses and scoring for sweeps. Related to Casino and Royal Casino.

content.text: Seep is a four-player partnership fishing game played in the Punjab and other parts of India and Pakistan. Players capture cards from a layout; building piles called houses and scoring for sweeps. Related to Casino and Royal Casino.

Country/Region of Origin: India, Pakistan (Punjab).
Time Period: Traditional; 30-point version is possibly older and very popular in the Punjab.
Historical Development: Fishing game related to Casino and Royal Casino; northern India version has 100-point total; Punjab version 30 points.
Cultural Significance: Popular partnership game in Punjab (India and Pakistan).
Four players in fixed partnerships (partners opposite). Deal and play counter-clockwise. Two-player variant exists.
Standard 52-card pack, no jokers. English pattern.
Standard 52-card deck, score sheet (optional), table space.

Dealer gives 4 cards to player on right and 4 face down on table. That player bids (9–13) and plays one card from the four; dealer then deals the rest in groups of four counter-clockwise. Bidder ends with 11 cards, others 12.

items.text: Two-Player Game: Four hands dealt; two to players, two face down. Play 12 cards each; remaining loose cards stay. Each player picks up one face-down hand and play continues. Transition is vulnerable to sweeps.
Limited Houses: Only two houses allowed on the floor at once. Creating a third is illegal; player must throw or pick up.
Scoring variation: 10♦ worth 2 instead of 6; 4 points for majority of cards (more than 26); total still 100. Some allow breaking a house with a floor card plus hand card to cement.

30-point Seep: Punjab version: 10♦=12, 9♠=9, 2♠=1, each ace=1; 4 for majority of cards (total 30). Sweep worth capture value of card played. Deal restarted if table has 10♦ or 9♠. Satthi (all 30 in one deal) = 60 points.
